tagline: From the Strait of Gibraltar to the Atlantic coast and the sheltered Med — a two-sea nation with a marina-and-crossing story.
summary: Morocco threads two seas: the Mediterranean north, where Tangier sits at the Strait of Gibraltar — one of the world's busiest passenger-sea crossings — and the calm Rif coast around Al Hoceima; and the Atlantic west, where Casablanca, the economic capital, fronts the ocean with the Rabat corridor running up the coast. It is a major port-and-tourism investor (Tangier Med, redeveloped marinas) with a clean fit for a foiling tier on the strait crossing, the urban bays and the calm Mediterranean coves.
why_marine_mobility: Morocco's water divides into three jobs: the short, dense Strait of Gibraltar crossing; the urban bays of Tangier and Casablanca; and the calm Mediterranean coves of Al Hoceima. Navier's Pioneer II flies the bays and coves — silent and zero-emission off redeveloped marinas — while the Quanta-LR's range and sea-keeping handle the exposed Strait crossing and the Atlantic Casablanca–Rabat corridor where an all-electric day-boat would be marginal.

demand_signals.label: Strait of Gibraltar crossing
demand_signals.note: One of the world's busiest passenger-sea corridors, with huge seasonal volumes on the ~16 nm Tangier–Tarifa link, including the massive Marhaba summer diaspora movement.

demand_signals.label: Casablanca–Rabat corridor
demand_signals.note: One of Morocco's densest intercity corridors links the economic and political capitals along the Atlantic coast — heavy road and rail demand paralleling an open coastal water route.

demand_signals.label: Marinas & coastal redevelopment
demand_signals.note: Tangier Marina, the Casablanca marina and the Al Hoceima bay anchor a growing waterfront leisure and property economy on both seas.

use_cases.body: A premium foiling tier on the short, dense Strait of Gibraltar crossing (Tangier–Tarifa) for the time-sensitive segment of a high-volume diesel-ferry market.
Urban-bay networks off the Tangier and Casablanca marinas, and calm Mediterranean cove-and-island runs around Al Hoceima.
A flagship Atlantic coastal corridor from Casablanca to Rabat on the Quanta-LR, whose sea-keeping handles the swell.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The urban-bay and Mediterranean-coast meshes — Tangier Marina↔Cap Spartel (~7 nm), Tangier↔Tanger Med (~24 nm), Casablanca↔Mohammedia (~13 nm), Al Hoceima↔Cala Iris/Bades (~14 nm) and bay hops — sit inside the 70 nm all-electric range off redeveloped marinas.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The exposed Strait of Gibraltar crossing (~16 nm, tidal, high-traffic) and the open-Atlantic Casablanca↔Rabat corridor (~46 nm) are Quanta-LR hybrid routes (H2 2026+) — the hybrid range and sea-keeping handle swell, currents and traffic with no charging dependency.

signature_routes.label: Tangier ↔ Tarifa — Strait of Gibraltar crossing (Quanta-LR)
Tangier Marina ↔ Cap Spartel (all-electric bay run)
Al Hoceima Marina ↔ Cala Iris / Bades islets (Mediterranean cove run)

transit_planning: For Tangier Med Port Authority, Morocco's National Ports Agency (ANP) or a marina operator: a clean tier combining a premium Strait crossing, urban-bay networks and calm Mediterranean leisure runs, aligned with Morocco's strong port-and-tourism investment agenda.
competitive_landscape: The Strait is served by large established diesel fast-ferries (FRS, Balearia, Inter Shipping) carrying enormous seasonal volumes — a real incumbent on the international crossing. Within the Moroccan bays and the Med coast there is no urban or coastal water transport, leaving greenfield room for a clean foiling tier.
regulatory_note: The Strait crossing engages Tangier Med Port Authority, Morocco's maritime administration and bilateral Morocco–Spain (EU/Schengen) arrangements. Urban and coastal activity falls under the ANP, with protected zones (Al Hoceima National Park) favouring low-wash, zero-emission craft. Morocco's port-and-tourism investment agenda is supportive.
seasonality: The Strait peaks massively in summer (June–September) with the Marhaba diaspora movement and runs year-round for trade; the urban-bay and Mediterranean-cove networks are summer-weighted. Strait tides and the Levante/Poniente winds, and Atlantic swell on the Casablanca coast, are the main constraints, where foiling stability and the Quanta-LR's sea-keeping help.
